text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000001 bills 99215 well above its risk-adjusted expectation, with a large share on low-complexity patients, but documentation is too thin to confirm or refute upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The risk-adjusted excess holds in every complexity band, and the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims are on routine presentations. Examples include isolated back pain (C0000332, C0000372, C0000574), urinary tract infection (C0000519, C0001539), follow-up visits (C0000309, C0001134) and upper respiratory infection (C0001605). That pattern is consistent with upcoding rather than a sicker panel, though sampled high-complexity 99215 claims such as C0000715 and C0000756 look appropriate. The records review cannot settle the question: only 2 documented 99215 claims came back, both supported (C0000268, C0000684), which is far too few to judge. The few notes claiming moderate-or-higher data reviewed with no lab or test line on the claim are weak evidence of templated notes, not proof. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims listed above to see whether MDM and time support level 5. Separately, they should check whether notes look cloned across visits."}
